title: A six-year-old boy sustains bullet wounds and a woman is missing in the two separate incidents in Naga-dominated Noney and Tamenglong districts
author: Rahul Karmakar
content_html:
Unidentified gunmen killed four civilians from the Kuki-Zo community, including two women, in two separate incidents in Manipur on Sunday (September 13, 2026).

Although no armed group claimed responsibility, Kuki-Zo organisations blamed the attacks on the National Socialist Council of Nagalim, or NSCN (Isak-Muivah), and the Zeliangrong United Front (Kamson).

Kuki-Zo organisations said the first attack was carried out around 4 a.m. at Tollen village in Tamenglong district. One Seineh Singsit and his wife Lhingzangai were killed, and their six-year-old son was injured.

The woman died on the spot, while her husband succumbed to his injuries at a nearby hospital. The minor is undergoing treatment with a bullet reportedly lodged inside his body.

The second incident occurred around 3 p.m. at Longpi village in Noney district. Local residents said the gunmen ambushed three persons transporting rice, killing two of them on the spot.

The deceased were identified as Julie Gangte and Thangroel Gangte. The third person, a woman, was reported missing.

Condemning the first attack, the Kuki Inpi JTN (Jiribam, Tamenglong, and Noney districts) said in a statement, “This inhuman act is not merely an attack on one family; it is an affront to humanity itself. Kuki Inpi JTN stands in solidarity with the bereaved family and calls for justice to be delivered without delay.”

The Western Village Volunteer (Jiribam, Tamenglong, and Noney), a Kuki-Zo organisation, demanded that the killers be identified, apprehended, and brought to justice within 24 hours. It warned that failing to ensure timely justice would compel it to “unleash all its anger to the perpetrators”.

Manipur Chief Minister Yumnam Khemchand Singh has expressed deep anguish over the killings. He said that such cowardly acts of violence against innocent civilians were unacceptable and have no place in society. The Chief Minister extended his condolences to the grieving families, praying for strength to the bereaved and a speedy recovery for the injured.

Appeal against shutdown

Meanwhile, the Manipur government appealed to the Campaign for Justice and Fair Delimitation to withdraw its ongoing shutdown of Central and State government offices to push for its demand to update the National Register of Citizens (NRC).

Government spokespersons Th. Radheyshyam and Sapam Ranjan Singh, both MLAs, said the campaign should not “add more misery to the sufferings and inconveniences” of the people of Manipur, who “also want the NRC to be conducted” before the Census exercise.

The government suggested that the campaign’s decision to intensify the pro-NRC agitation was unjust after the Union Ministry of Home Affairs postponed the Census process in Manipur. The spokespersons also pointed out that the Manipur Assembly favoured 1951 as the base year for updating the NRC, as most Manipur inhabitants wanted.

title: Want to 'reset' ties with India, should be done through bilateral discussions: Bangladesh
author: PTI
content_html:
Bangladesh on Sunday (September 13, 2026) said it wants to “reset” its relationship with India and build a new bilateral engagement based on mutual interests, while describing ties during the tenure of deposed Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina as “uncomfortable”.

The remarks by State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humaiun Kobir came two days after Bangladesh said Prime Minister Tarique Rahman would not participate in the BRICS Summit hosted by India as he was not invited to the event, with the invitation instead extended to the BIMSTEC chair.

The two-day BRICS Summit concluded on Sunday (September 13, 2026). India had invited Mr. Rahman to attend the summit as chairperson of the Bay of Bengal Initiative for Multi-Sectoral Technical and Economic Cooperation (BIMSTEC), while a separate bilateral invitation had been in place since February.

Bangladesh wants to “reset” its bilateral relationship with India, Mr. Kobir told reporters. “We want to move towards a new relationship, which should be done through bilateral discussions, not through a multilateral forum,” he said.

India-Bangladesh ties have been strained over New Delhi providing refuge to Hasina, who fled to India following her ouster in a youth-led agitation in August 2024.

Mr. Kobir said Bangladesh needs to move beyond what he described as an “excessive preoccupation” with India and approach its relationship with New Delhi in a balanced manner, focusing on mutual interests and treating it as part of its broader engagement with other countries.

“We have to get out of the India fascination. India is just another country, and Bangladesh wants good bilateral relations with it,” he said.

Responding to a question, the Minister said, “Breakfast in India, lunch in India, dinner in India — then when will you eat your own food?” Mr. Kobir also said Prime Minister Rahman is scheduled to leave for New York on September 21 to attend the 81st session of the UN General Assembly and stay there until September 26.

Asked about the possibility of a meeting between Mr. Rahman and U.S. President Donald Trump on the sidelines of the UNGA, he said such meetings are often decided at the last moment during major international conferences.

“The primary focus of the Prime Minister’s visit is to address the UN General Assembly,” Mr. Kobir said, adding that details of the sideline meetings would be known in due course.

title: Indian missing after attack on Panama-flagged tanker off Oman; MEA says search ops. on
author: PTI
content_html:
India on Sunday (September 13, 2026) condemned an attack on a Panama-flagged oil tanker off the coast of Oman that resulted in one Indian seafarer being reported missing.

The Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) said 13 other Indian crew members of the vessel, MT El Gaia, were rescued.

"We condemn the attack on the commercial vessel MT El Gaia off the coast of Oman earlier today. Of the 14 Indian crew onboard, 13 Indians have been rescued so far," it said.

Our statement on the attack on a commercial vessel off the coast of Oman ⬇️

🔗 https://t.co/u78n9UGNFFpic.twitter.com/RjCOaDMQQL

— Randhir Jaiswal (@MEAIndia) September 13, 2026

"Search and rescue operations for the missing Indian national are continuing. Our embassy in Oman is closely monitoring the situation and proactively coordinating with the Omani authorities in the ongoing search and rescue operation," the MEA said in a statement.

The Indian side thanked Omani authorities for their support in rescuing the Indian seafarers. "We reiterate our call for immediate de-escalation of tensions and pursuance of dialogue and diplomacy to bring peace to the region," the MEA said.

"The targeting of commercial shipping, seafarers, civilians, and civilian infrastructure in the region is unacceptable," it added.

New Delhi has been concerned over attacks on commercial shipping as most of the vessels usually have Indian seafarers.

Speaking at the BRICS summit on Saturday (September 13, 2026), Prime Minister Narendra Modi proposed the creation of a "Seafarers' Emergency Support Network" to safeguard them from security risks due to regional conflicts.

Ten Indian seafarers are among the 16 Indians killed so far in the West Asia conflict, while another five Indian seafarers have died in strikes on merchant vessels in the Black Sea. "We also urge that free and safe navigation and flow of commerce through the international waterways in the region be restored at the earliest," the MEA said.

title: BJP imposing its 'deeply problematic' dietary preferences on foreign dignitaries, says Congress on BRICS dinner
author: PTI
content_html:
A day after an all-vegetarian spread was served at a BRICS Summit gala dinner, the Congress on Sunday said the BJP was now imposing its "deeply problematic" dietary preferences on dignitaries from across the world, with Leader of the Opposition Rahul Gandhi pointing out that 80% of Indians are non-vegetarian.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi hosted the dinner for the leaders and delegates of the BRICS Summit at the Bharat Mandapam on Saturday (September 12, 2026).

In a post on social media platforms X, Facebook and Instagram, Mr. Gandhi wrote, "For the record: 80% of Indians are non-vegetarian. Indian non-vegetarian food is delicious. As are my sister's chole bhature." He also posted a picture of chole bhature on a dining table.

While Mr. Gandhi made no direct reference to the BRICS dinner, Congress's media and publicity department head Pawan Khera shared the screenshot of the menu from the dinner and attacked the BJP.

"The BJP's habit of imposing its dietary preferences on fellow Indians is already deeply problematic. Now, they have taken it a step further by imposing their own choices on dignitaries from across the world," Mr. Khera said on X.

“India is a rich, diverse, multi-cuisine country, home to some of the finest non-vegetarian delicacies that people across the world relish and enjoy,” he said.

For the record: 80% of Indians are non-vegetarian.

Indian non-vegetarian food is delicious. As are my sister's chole bhature. pic.twitter.com/8f6ziKjLan

— Rahul Gandhi (@RahulGandhi) September 13, 2026

“So why did the Modi government choose to hide this part of India's culture,” Mr. Khera asked."Is it ashamed of the diversity that makes India what it is," the Congress leader asked.

Rijiju slams Congress

BJP leader and Union Minister Kiren Rijiju lashed out at the Congress for its criticism. "I can't believe that the Congress party is making politics even on the food menu served to the leaders of BRICS nations. Our guests relished Indian vegetarian cuisine which are rich in flavour and nutritional variety with diverse regional traditions," Mr. Rijiju said.

BJP national spokesperson Pradeep Bhandari said, "When the Opposition has nothing except the food menu to criticise about the summit, it tells you how successful BRICS has been." "Congress is sulking to see India emerge as a global consensus builder," he wrote on X.

Congress' social media head Supriya Shrinate hailed Mr. Gandhi's post and said it defines who he is.

"It stands out for two things: respect for India's diversity; respect for people's choices including what they eat," she said on X.

"That apart, what is a Sunday without yummy lip-smacking chola bhatura?!" she said.

Congress spokesperson Shama Mohamed shared the screenshot of the menu and took a swipe at the government over the issue.

"No wonder Xi Jinping went back to his hotel for dinner. I would do the same!" she said on X.

Srivatsa, a close aide of Mr. Gandhi, said foreign dignitaries would have to wait till 2029 to have delicious Indian food of all kinds. "Sabka Khana, Sabke Saath," he added.

In another post, Mr. Srivatsa said one post from LoP Rahul Gandhi — one fact, one photograph of his lunch and the entire discourse had moved from where the BJP wanted it to where Mr. Gandhi put it.

"And it's a debate this country has needed for a long time. For over a decade, a manufactured vegetarian orthodoxy has been imposed on a nation by the BJP where 80% of people eat meat. Look at what they are doing in States like Bengal and Bihar recently," he said.

Mr. Gandhi has "exposed, with one fact and a plate of food, not a debate about diet, but a debate about who gets to decide how 150 crore Indians live, and what they choose to eat", Mr. Srivatsa said on X.

Earlier, in a post on X on Saturday night, Mahua Moitra said, "Would I be a bad MP if I advised the visiting BRICS leaders to give this menu a miss & get security to nip down to the nearest Karims & bring back some Burrab Kababs." The gala dinner featured an elaborate all-vegetarian menu. 'Khandvi mille', a feuille steamed gram-flour roll, and 'khumb galouti', pan-grilled mushroom kebabs with mint pearls, were served as starters.

The main course offered 'paneer lababdar', 'gucchi marmik' — Himalayan morel mushrooms and tender asparagus — and 'carrot bean poriyal'.

The other items on the menu included 'thakkali belle saaru' — light lentil broth, millet pulao, beetroot raita and assorted Indian breads.

For the desserts, 'Old Delhi fruit cream with jalebi' and 'shahtoot phirni' wrapped up the menu for the VVIP guests.

title: Centre treating Bihar as stepchild: Tejashwi Yadav on flood-related issues
author: Amit Bhelari
content_html:
Leader of the Opposition in Bihar Tejashwi Yadav on Sunday (September 13, 2026) slammed both the State and central government over the lack of seriousness in dealing with the recent Bihar floods, claiming that the State is being treated like a “stepchild”.

Mr. Yadav, who is the Rashtriya Janata Dal (RJD) National Working President, said he had written to Prime Minister Narendra Modi demanding that the Bihar floods be declared a national disaster, and also sought compensation and a special economic package for affected families. The Central government has not shown any seriousness in this regard so far, he said.

Over 48 lakh people are affected by the floods, Mr. Yadav said, adding that he had also written to Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary, but to no avail. Mr. Yadav alleged that the ‘double-engine’ government in Bihar is not serious about this issue and that both engines have caught fire, preventing people from receiving aid. There has been no hearing or action taken yet, he added.

The RJD leader asserted that although there are eight NDA Ministers and 30 Lok Sabha MPs from Bihar, the people of the State have been left to deal with the situation by themselves.

“The state government withdrew ₹4,000 crore from the Contingency Fund in July and utilised the money for salaries and other administrative expenses. Bihar’s treasury is empty, and the Central Government ministers from the state lack the clout to secure central assistance,” Mr. Yadav said.

He added that during the Kosi floods (2008), his father and then Union Minister for Railways Lalu Prasad had secured a special package for Bihar. “At that time, Prime Minister Manmohan Singh ji and Congress National President Sonia Gandhi ji visited Bihar to provide relief funds and ensure justice for the Kosi flood victims. In contrast, the attitude of the Narendra Modi government towards Bihar reveals their mindset,”Mr. Yadav said.

He further claimed that in Gujarat, even if there is rainfall, the government immediately sets up relief camps and provides all possible assistance, including a package to the State.

Mr. Yadav also alleged that leaders of the BJP and the central government always ignore the people of Bihar during times of disaster, and when election season comes, everyone from the Prime Minister to the Home Minister starts visiting to seek votes.

“Bihar is being treated like a stepchild, as no assistance is received from BJP-ruled states. During elections, Amit Shah speaks of making Bihar flood-free; however, when more than 47 lakh people are trapped in the devastation of the floods—he is nowhere to be found, not even issuing a single statement. This attitude reveals the nature of the Centre and State’s conduct towards Bihar; those in power are simply not serious about this issue,” Mr. Yadav said.

He claimed that when he visited the flood-affected areas to meet the victims, the boat he was given by State Disaster Response Force (SDRF) began to deflate in the middle of the river, and villagers had to rescue him.

Mr. Yadav said that in his capacity as the Leader of the Opposition, he assessed the situation and demanded that the government should provide aid and financial assistance to the flood victims.

According to the Bihar Disaster Management Department (DMD), over 48.35 lakh people were affected by floods in 87 blocks of 15 districts.

title: Keralam CM V.D. Satheesan takes a trip down memory lane at alumni meet
author: The Hindu Bureau
content_html:
Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan on Sunday (September 13) took a trip down memory lane, recalling how his days at Panangad High School helped shape his communication skills.

Addressing an alumni meeting at his alma mater, the Chief Minister said that it was at the school that he “learned to speak”. He said the foundation in English that he acquired at the Malayalam-medium school gave him the confidence to deliver speeches in the language later, including a lecture at Harvard University.

“Standing here today, I’m at a loss for words. It was the teachers here who encouraged me to read and learn. When I joined SH College after completing my schooling here, I felt an inferiority complex while listening to other students speak English fluently. However, after listening to them keenly, I realised that they were making many grammatical errors, while our teachers here had taught us grammar thoroughly. That gave me the confidence to speak in English,” he said.

Kerala High Court judge Devan Ramachandran inaugurated the meet attended by Ministers N. Samsudheen, Roji M. John, V.E Abdul Gafoor, Hibi Eden, MP, and Deputy Speaker Shanimol Osman, among others.
